# How a story plays

A story is a graph of beats (checkpoints) joined by exits (transitions). Each exit has a condition (a gate) over the story's tracked facts (qualities). Exactly one beat is active at a time.

After each reply the reading model reads the recent chat and proposes changes to the qualities, each backed by a quoted line. The changes are applied at the next turn boundary, after a reply has finished. Then the exits of the active beat are checked; when one opens, the story moves to the next beat and that beat's effects run (lore switches on, the cast changes, a background appears, a character speaks). One exit fires per turn.

The story bar reports setup progress while the scene's cast is saved together, and elapsed time when a model call
takes more than ten seconds. Pending illustration and character work has a placeholder above the input. Slow
action buttons stay busy until their work finishes; these indicators need no story fields.

Beside the chat (no story fields): the story bar above the input names the scene (the beat's `player_name`, else the open chapter, else the story title), shows tension as five dots and a word, and on its right at most one status chip and the story sheet button. The chip says what reading is waiting on when the story knows ("waiting for a character" while a character's inner beat holds the read); a read still running after two minutes reads "catching up…" and the chip opens the story card with Try again, which checks on the running read and never starts a second one. The scene opens the story card above it: where you are, the status line (Try again or Settings when there is something to do), what you notice, one button per story sheet page and Story window. In Author view the card also holds the notes level for this chat.

The story sheet is one window with a tab per page the story has: Journal (quests, log and what you noticed; a log row's arrow scrolls the chat to its message), Here now (see Scene card), People & places, Stats (the value large, the label beside it), one tab per story panel, Ideas (What could I do?) and Memory (a few things the story remembers, with Open memory). On a wide window it docks to the right of the chat (drag its left edge to change the width, which is remembered) and can pop out into a movable window; on a phone it is a bottom sheet above the input with three heights (small, half, full; drag the grip or press it), and the half height stops short of the last reply so it stays readable. The wand menu holds Story sheet, Story recap, Flag this moment, the story window and Help.

Notes under messages: at the player levels a reply carries at most one quiet line of words, such as "The story moved on · Remembered 2 things"; hovering a part names its category, and clicking the line opens the notes grouped by category. What each category and level means is explained under the level picker (Settings › Interface) and in Help. Author (3) adds details, actions and an Inspect link; Raw (4) adds a raw count per category, and raw data stays in the inspector. Help lists every part of Story Orchestrator in one searchable list grouped by who it is for, each row with a plain "Where:" line and Show me.

Two things follow, and most of the advice below comes from them:

- **The story only knows what the chat shows.** A gate on a thought, a mood or something that happened off screen never opens, because nobody can quote it.
- **The chat can be rewound.** Swipes, edits and deletions roll the story back. Effects are rebuilt from the path the chat took, so they must depend on the path, never on the clock.

A player line that is wholly out of character (wrapped in `((…))`, or starting `OOC:` / `(OOC`) stays in the chat the narrator sees, but the reading model is never shown it: it sets no quality, fact or memory, and it is no player turn for open-stretch pace, agendas or a refused route (`src/engine/ooc.ts`). A continuity note waiting for review does not lapse on it, and the story panel's log does not list it. Tell players to correct the story with an edit, not an OOC line.
